title: Proactive node refurbishment and SLO‑hedged maintenance windows for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: For Dedicated customers we currently perform node lifecycle work (kernel updates, disk refresh, NIC firmware) in large maintenance waves that assume static capacity hedges. This causes transient SLO regressions when maintenance collides with unexpected workload spikes or when KV cache warmup times are long.

Goal: Build a proactive node refurbishment workflow that (1) automatically identifies candidate nodes for maintenance based on device health signals and usage patterns, (2) schedules maintenance within flexible SLO‑hedged windows that adapt to current cluster load and reserved throughput commitments, and (3) performs rolling replacement with KV cache preservation and traffic smoothing to keep tail latency and throughput within contract guarantees.

Scope: Dedicated fleets (reserved capacity) only. The feature includes: node scoring, adaptive maintenance window scheduler, preheat/replicate KV cache step, traffic shedding and burst lanes with autoscale hedges, graceful drain/decommission state machine, and console controls for operators and customers to opt into maintenance urgency levels.

Out‑of‑scope for this ticket: UI polish for console controls (will be linked PRD), private deployment air‑gapped install automation, and persistent data migration tooling (separate disk migration epic).
acceptance_criteria: A node scoring daemon (agent) publishes candidate nodes with scores > threshold to FleetControl API and is discoverable via fleet diagnostics.

Maintenance scheduler reserves a dynamic hedged throughput lane that matches customer reserved capacity + buffer and only starts a maintenance wave if hedged capacity is available or autoscale hedges are provisioned.
Rolling replacements maintain 99th percentile latency within SLA (as measured by synthetic canaries and production traffic for test accounts) across a 4 hour maintenance window testbed.
KV cache snapshot + preheat step reduces cold‑start request penalty by >= 60% on average for warmed partitions compared to uncontrolled drains.
Operator can pause, abort, or accelerate an ongoing maintenance wave from Console or fleet API; abort causes graceful reintegration without data loss.
Automated playbook logs and a post‑wave summary report are created and uploaded to the customer retention bucket for audit purposes.
design_decisions: Use an out‑of‑process node scoring agent to avoid coupling with the runtime hot path; scoring inputs include hardware telemetry, pod eviction rate, recent preemptions, and disk SMART metrics.
Scheduler will prefer low‑traffic AZ windows and use predictive demand smoothing from the forecast service (runtime demand model) to select start times.
KV cache preservation will use a lightweight serialized prefix checkpoint per worker and a background preheat utility on target nodes to reduce cold misses.

Autoscale hedges: the scheduler will create short‑lived burst leases that temporarily raise capacity (billed to customer/buffer) instead of immediate global scale events to avoid destabilizing other tenants.
Traffic smoothing employs a token‑bucket ramp for evicted connections to bound request drop and allow graceful failover to fallback model variants.
Default policy is conservative (low urgency); customers can select expedited modes with different billing/impact tradeoffs.
implementation_notes: Components: node‑scorer (agent), maintenance‑scheduler service, fleetcontrol API extensions, drain state machine, kv‑checkpoint service, preheat workers, autoscale‑hedge manager, console toggle endpoints.
Phases: 1) agent + scoring + telemetry ingestion, 2) scheduler + hedging contract, 3) KV checkpoint + preheat integration, 4) canary testing on internal reserved fleet, 5) customer pilot, 6) GA.

Canary plan: Run on internal dev‑dedicated clusters with synthetic workloads and one non‑critical customer fleet as pilot; start at 2 nodes per wave and ramp to full wave size after 72h of stable metrics.
Telemetry: add maintenance_wave_id tag to existing latency/cost traces, expose preheat hit rate metric, and create alert on hedged_capacity_shortfall.
Rollback: if 99p latency exceeds threshold for longer than perturbation_window (10m), automatically pause the wave and begin reintegration steps.
test_plan: Unit tests for node scorer thresholds and scheduler decision logic.
Integration tests that simulate different load scenarios (sudden spike, gradual ramp, long‑tail KV cache warmup) in CI harness.
Chaos tests: induce worker failures during preheat and verify graceful fallback without SLO violation.
Load test: synthetic skyline workload that verifies throughput guarantees under maintenance with hedges enabled.
Compliance test: ensure audit log entries for maintenance waves meet retention schema and include operator identity.
monitoring_and_metrics: Metrics to add: maintenance_wave_count, maintenance_wave_duration_seconds, hedged_capacity_utilization, kv_preheat_hit_ratio, drain_eviction_latency_percentiles, maintenance_abort_rate.
Dashboards: maintenance overview with per‑fleet active waves, preheat effectiveness, and hedged lane consumption.
Alerts: maintenance_wave_failure (SLO breach), hedged_capacity_shortfall, preheat_failure_rate > 5% over 10m.
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal dev fleet canary (manual approvals), collect preheat metrics and refine thresholds.
Week 2–3: pilot with 1–3 opt‑in customers; provide playbook and runbook with SEs on standby.
Week 4: open beta for all dedicated customers with UI controls hidden (API opt‑in).
Week 6: GA with Console toggle and billing hooks for expedited modes.
Post‑GA: iterate on heuristics and integrate with Optimize for recommended hedging parameters.
notes: PM (Jonah Kim) requested adjustable urgency levels for enterprise customers during contract negotiations.
SRE: ensure the hedged leases do not starve shared-hosted capacity; billing team to confirm chargeback model.
Follow‑up: tie preheat effectiveness into Optimize so customers get suggested preheat sizes based on historical prefix hits.
